title: When the Prom Breaks
premise: Dominic Crane has survived twenty years in the small town of Harrow Bend by being careful, invisible, and endlessly agreeable—until a group chat called The Ledger begins posting predictions that come true with unsettling precision, including one about her. As the messages escalate, Dominic realizes they point toward something the school board buried decades ago: a fire, a missing student, and a cover-up that explains why her family's name carries so much quiet weight in town. Racing the last football game of the season, when the final prediction is due to land, she must choose between protecting the people who kept her safe and telling the truth that will burn every bridge she has. In the end, Dominic exposes the buried record at the homecoming assembly, losing her best friend's loyalty but gaining, for the first time, a town that actually sees her—and a future she chooses instead of inherits.
about_author: Ulyana Galloway grew up in a farming town smaller than the one she writes about, where everyone knew her business before she did. She now lives near a lake with two dogs and an unhealthy collection of yearbooks from towns she's never visited.

chapters.title: The Careful Life
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. We meet Harrow Bend through her morning routine: the practiced laugh at practice jokes, the edited self, the twenty-year habit of staying small. Her best friend Priya drags her to a bonfire where someone mentions a strange group chat. Emotional beat: the ache of belonging somewhere that doesn't fully know you.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Witnesses
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She's added to The Ledger against her will—a chat of forty classmates posting predictions: game scores, breakups, a teacher's resignation. All accurate. When a prediction names her, 'the Crane kid finally speaks,' she dismisses it as a prank. Emotional beat: unease disguised as irritation; the first crack in her armor of control.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Kept
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Cleaning her late grandmother's attic for inheritance paperwork, she finds a scorched 1978 yearbook with a student's photo blacked out and a key labeled H.B.H.S.—Records. A Ledger message arrives: 'Ask what burned.' Emotional beat: dread braided with curiosity; the past reaching into the present.

chapters.title: Priya's Price
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Dominic and Priya. Priya, whose father sits on the school board, warns Dominic to drop it—the Cranes have always known when to stay quiet. Their friendship strains over dinner. Meanwhile another prediction comes true exactly. Emotional beat: loyalty revealed as a cage, not just a comfort.

chapters.title: The Locked Room
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Using the key, she gets into the school's old records annex after hours and finds a sealed file on Danny Okafor, a student who 'transferred' in 1978—the same night as the gymnasium fire. The file is thin. Too thin. Someone got there first. Emotional beat: the thrill of discovery curdling into fear of being watched.

chapters.title: Predictions
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs via chat transcripts and classroom scenes. The Ledger escalates: it predicts a locker vandalism targeting Dominic, and it happens within hours. Classmates who ignored her start treating her like an omen. She realizes the predictions aren't supernatural—they're someone testing how much truth the town can absorb. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Buried
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She tracks down Danny Okafor's sister, now living two counties away, who reveals Danny died in the fire and the board covered it up to protect a beloved coach—and that Dominic's grandmother helped bury the record to save the school, and the town, from collapse. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger, betrayal by blood, the weight of inherited silence.

chapters.title: Last Game of the Season
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Homecoming week. The Ledger posts its final prediction: 'Friday night, the whole town hears the truth.' Priya must decide whether to warn her father or stand with Dominic. She chooses neither—she goes silent, and Dominic learns the chat's admin is someone unexpected: the school secretary, Danny's childhood friend, finishing what she couldn't do in 1978. Emotional beat: loyalty fracturing into something more honest.

chapters.title: The Assembly
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the homecoming assembly, with the gym full—the same gym that burned—Dominic takes the microphone and reads Danny Okafor's name aloud, then her grandmother's role in the cover-up, sacrificing her family's clean legacy. The room erupts; the board members walk out; Priya stands up beside her anyway. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into liberation; visibility as an act of love.

chapters.title: After the Prom Breaks
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, weeks later. The investigation reopens; the town is raw but talking—for the first time, honestly. Dominic plants a memorial tree for Danny with the secretary and repairs her friendship with Priya on new terms. She applies to colleges far away, not to escape, but because leaving is now a choice, not a flight. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope; belonging rebuilt on truth.
